title: Placement of the endotracheal tube using Electrical Impedance Tomography in pediatric patients (EnTubEIT study).
summary:
The correct placement of the breathing tube (endotracheal tube) is very important in preterm infants, newborns, and children. If the tube is not positioned correctly, one lung may not be adequately ventilated or excessive pressure may be generated. This can worsen breathing and potentially damage the lungs.
Despite existing guidelines, there remains a risk that the breathing tube in newborns and children—especially in preterm infants—may not be optimally positioned. Therefore, more reliable methods are needed to ensure correct placement already during insertion.

The aim of this study is to investigate, in approximately 60 children, whether additional monitoring using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT) during insertion of the breathing tube can help prevent misplacement.

For this purpose, your child will be fitted with a soft, elastic belt around the chest. This allows us to monitor lung ventilation painlessly and without the use of X-ray radiation.

We consider this project to be very important, as correct placement of the breathing tube can significantly improve the safety of newborns and children.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All preterm infants, term newborns, and children undergoing an elective surgical procedure with planned intubation anesthesia may be included in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Patients receiving palliative care
2) Patients with known malformations of the airways (larynx and trachea/bronchi)
3) Lack of parental consent prior to the elective procedure
4) Contraindication to performing EIT measurement according to approval (e.g., presence of a pacemaker) or inability to perform EIT measurement on the thorax due to wound dressings or indwelling drains.
